records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁל֗וֹשׁ לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס דָּבָר֙ נִגְלָ֣ה לְדָֽנִיֵּ֔אל אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֑ר וֶאֱמֶ֤ת הַדָּבָר֙ וְצָבָ֣א גָד֔וֹל וּבִין֙ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֔ר וּבִ֥ינָה ל֖וֹ בַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: In year three of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar; and true [was] the word, and a great conflict; and he understood the word, and understanding [was] to him in the vision.
pieces: In the third year of the reign of Cyrus king of Persia, a message was made known to Daniel, who had been given the name Belteshazzar. The message was true, and it was about a great war. He understood the message; he was given understanding in the vision.

L.1: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar. And the word was true, and [it concerned] a great conflict. And he understood the word and had understanding of the vision.

R.1: In Cyrus's third year as king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, who was also called Belteshazzar. The message was true. It was about a great war. Daniel understood the message. He understood what the vision meant.

decisions.choice: the third year of Cyrus: about 536 BC, the last date in the book
decisions.reason: Cyrus took Babylon in 539 BC, and his first year over it was counted from 538 (Ezra 1:1). His third year is about 536 BC. Daniel had served from the first year of Nebuchadnezzar to the first year of Cyrus (1:21); this is his last vision, and the longest. Chapters 10-12 are one vision: this chapter introduces it, 11:2-12:4 gives the message, and 12:5-13 ends it.

decisions.choice: Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar
decisions.reason: Belteshazzar is the Babylonian name given to Daniel at the court (1:7). Here, in the time of the Persians, the narrator reminds the reader of it. The verse speaks of Daniel in the third person; from verse 2 he tells the vision himself.

decisions.choice: a great conflict: a great war, or great hardship
decisions.reason: The word is the one for an army or warfare, and so for hard service (Isaiah 40:2; Job 7:1). The message concerns a great conflict: the wars of chapter 11 and the struggle in heaven of 10:13, 20-21, or the hardship they bring.

decisions.choice: in the third year of the reign of Cyrus (B); in Cyrus's third year as king (R)
decisions.reason: The date follows the wording set for dated headings in Jeremiah. Readable adds "also" for the second name.

records.heading: A vision by the Tigris

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֖ים הָהֵ֑ם אֲנִ֤י דָֽנִיֵּאל֙ הָיִ֣יתִי מִתְאַבֵּ֔ל שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה שָׁבֻעִ֖ים יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: In the days those I, Daniel, was mourning three sevens of days.
pieces: At that time I, Daniel, had been mourning for three whole weeks.

L.2: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks of days.

R.2: At that time I, Daniel, had been very sad for three weeks.

decisions.choice: three weeks of days: three full weeks
decisions.reason: The word for "weeks" is the word "sevens" of 9:24-27. Here "of days" is added to make plain that these are weeks of days, perhaps to set them apart from the sevens of chapter 9.

decisions.choice: mourning: fasting and sorrow, perhaps for the state of the returned exiles
decisions.reason: Daniel does not say why he mourned. The return under Cyrus had begun (Ezra 1-3), but in about 536 BC the rebuilding of the temple met opposition and stopped (Ezra 4:4-5, 24). His mourning is a time of prayer and humbling himself (verse 12).

decisions.choice: weeks (all levels)
decisions.reason: Here the unit is stated ("of days"), so every level says "weeks"; in 9:24-27, where no unit is given, the word is "sevens".

records.source: לֶ֣חֶם חֲמֻד֞וֹת לֹ֣א אָכַ֗לְתִּי וּבָשָׂ֥ר וָיַ֛יִן לֹא־בָ֥א אֶל־פִּ֖י וְס֣וֹךְ לֹא־סָ֑כְתִּי עַד־מְלֹ֕את שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת שָׁבֻעִ֖ים יָמִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: Food of desirablenesses not I ate, and meat and wine not came into my mouth, and anointing not I anointed myself, until were completed three sevens of days.
pieces: I ate no fine food; no meat or wine passed my lips, and I did not put any oil on myself until the three weeks were over.

L.3: I ate no pleasant food, and no meat or wine came into my mouth, and I did not anoint myself at all, until the three weeks of days were completed.

R.3: I did not eat any rich food. I did not eat any meat or drink any wine. I did not put any lotion on my skin until those three weeks were over.

decisions.choice: anoint myself: rub oil on the skin
decisions.reason: Olive oil was rubbed on the skin and hair to refresh it and to keep it from drying in the heat (Ruth 3:3; 2 Samuel 14:2; Matthew 6:17). Leaving it off was a sign of mourning.

decisions.choice: pleasant food: rich, choice food
decisions.reason: "Food of desires" is the good food one would enjoy, as against plain food. Daniel's fast was partial, as his diet of vegetables was in 1:12.

decisions.choice: put any oil on myself (B); put any lotion on my skin (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "anoint"; Balanced and Readable say what it was (m1), since "anoint" suggests a religious rite to a modern reader.

records.source: וּבְי֛וֹם עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וַאֲנִ֗י הָיִ֛יתִי עַ֣ל יַ֧ד הַנָּהָ֛ר הַגָּד֖וֹל ה֥וּא חִדָּֽקֶל׃
records.gloss: And on day twenty and four of the month the first, and I was on [the] side of the river the great, it [is] Hiddekel,
pieces: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, the Tigris.

L.4: And on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, while I was by the side of the great river, that is, the Tigris,

R.4: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing beside the great Tigris River.

decisions.choice: the twenty-fourth day of the first month: in the spring, just after Passover
decisions.reason: The first month, Nisan, is in March-April. Passover fell on the fourteenth day, with the Festival of Unleavened Bread from the fifteenth to the twenty-first (Leviticus 23:5-6). Daniel's three weeks of fasting would have run through the festival days.

decisions.choice: the great river, the Tigris: the Hebrew name is Hiddekel
decisions.reason: Hiddekel is the Hebrew name of the Tigris, one of the four rivers of Eden (Genesis 2:14). Elsewhere "the great river" is the Euphrates (Genesis 15:18), but here it is said to be the Tigris, which flows past Babylon to the east. Some ancient translations read the Euphrates here.

decisions.choice: the Tigris (all levels)
decisions.reason: Every level uses the familiar name for Hiddekel (m2). Literal ends with a comma, since the sentence runs into verse 5.

records.heading: The man clothed in linen

records.source: וָאֶשָּׂ֤א אֶת־עֵינַי֙ וָאֵ֔רֶא וְהִנֵּ֥ה אִישׁ־אֶחָ֖ד לָב֣וּשׁ בַּדִּ֑ים וּמָתְנָ֥יו חֲגֻרִ֖ים בְּכֶ֥תֶם אוּפָֽז׃
records.gloss: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a man, one, clothed [in] linen, and his loins girded with gold of Uphaz.
pieces: I looked up and saw a man dressed in linen, wearing around his waist a belt of fine gold from Uphaz.

L.5: I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a man clothed in linen, and his waist was girded with gold of Uphaz.

R.5: I looked up and saw a man dressed in linen clothes. He had a belt of pure gold around his waist.

decisions.choice: a man clothed in linen: a heavenly being
decisions.reason: The man clothed in linen is like the one in Ezekiel's vision who marks the faithful (Ezekiel 9:2-3; 10:2) and like the angel of 12:6-7. Linen is the dress of priests (Leviticus 16:4) and of heavenly beings. He is not named. Most read him as an angel, perhaps Gabriel, who goes on to speak in verses 11-14 and needs Michael's help (verse 13); some read the glorious figure of verses 5-6 as a different and greater being than the one who speaks, and Christian readers have often seen a likeness to the risen Christ of Revelation 1:13-15. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: gold of Uphaz: fine gold
decisions.reason: Uphaz is named again only in Jeremiah 10:9 as a source of gold. Its place is unknown; some take it as a form of Ophir, famous for its gold (1 Kings 9:28).

decisions.choice: a man; his (no deity pronoun)
decisions.reason: The figure is described as a man, as Gabriel is in 9:21, and the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, since he is a heavenly messenger (m1). Readable says "pure gold" for gold of Uphaz.

records.source: וּגְוִיָּת֣וֹ כְתַרְשִׁ֗ישׁ וּפָנָ֞יו כְּמַרְאֵ֤ה בָרָק֙ וְעֵינָיו֙ כְּלַפִּ֣ידֵי אֵ֔שׁ וּזְרֹֽעֹתָיו֙ וּמַרְגְּלֹתָ֔יו כְּעֵ֖ין נְחֹ֣שֶׁת קָלָ֑ל וְק֥וֹל דְּבָרָ֖יו כְּק֥וֹל הָמֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And his body [was] like chrysolite, and his face like [the] appearance of lightning, and his eyes like torches of fire, and his arms and his feet like [the] gleam of bronze burnished, and the sound of his words like [the] sound of a multitude.
pieces: His body shone like chrysolite, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, and his arms and legs gleamed like polished bronze. His voice sounded like the noise of a great crowd.

L.6: And his body was like chrysolite, and his face like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes like torches of fire, and his arms and his feet like the gleam of polished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.

R.6: His body shone like a precious stone. His face was as bright as lightning, and his eyes were like flaming torches. His arms and legs shone like polished bronze. When he spoke, his voice sounded like a huge crowd of people.

decisions.choice: chrysolite: a gold-colored precious stone
decisions.reason: The stone is named after Tarshish. It is one of the stones of the high priest's breastplate (Exodus 28:20) and of the wheels in Ezekiel's vision (Ezekiel 1:16; 10:9). Which stone it is is not certain: chrysolite, beryl or topaz have been suggested.

decisions.choice: eyes like torches, limbs like bronze, a voice like a multitude: Ezekiel 1 and Revelation 1
decisions.reason: The description recalls the living creatures and the glory of Ezekiel 1:7, 13-14, 24, and is echoed in the risen Jesus of Revelation 1:14-15, whose eyes are "like a flame of fire" and feet "like burnished bronze".

decisions.choice: legs (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for feet is used of the legs as well (as in Ezekiel 1:7); Balanced and Readable say "legs", the limb that would gleam with the arms. Readable says "a precious stone" for chrysolite (m1).

records.source: וְרָאִיתִי֩ אֲנִ֨י דָנִיֵּ֤אל לְבַדִּי֙ אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֔ה וְהָאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֣וּ עִמִּ֔י לֹ֥א רָא֖וּ אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֑ה אֲבָ֗ל חֲרָדָ֤ה גְדֹלָה֙ נָפְלָ֣ה עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַֽיִּבְרְח֖וּ בְּהֵחָבֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And I saw, I, Daniel, I alone, the vision, and the men who were with me not saw the vision, but trembling great fell on them, and they fled in hiding themselves.
pieces: I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see it, but such terror came over them that they ran away and hid.

L.7: And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, and the men who were with me did not see the vision; but a great trembling fell upon them, and they fled to hide themselves.

R.7: I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see it. But they were so frightened that they ran away and hid.

decisions.choice: the men with me did not see the vision: compare Acts 9:7
decisions.reason: When the risen Jesus appeared to Paul, the men with him heard a sound but saw no one (Acts 9:7; 22:9). Here Daniel's companions see nothing but feel the presence and flee.

decisions.choice: such terror came over them (B); they were so frightened (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "a great trembling fell upon them"; Balanced and Readable say it in plain words.

records.source: וַאֲנִי֙ נִשְׁאַ֣רְתִּי לְבַדִּ֔י וָֽאֶרְאֶ֗ה אֶת־הַמַּרְאָ֤ה הַגְּדֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹ֥א נִשְׁאַר־בִּ֖י כֹּ֑ח וְהוֹדִ֗י נֶהְפַּ֤ךְ עָלַי֙ לְמַשְׁחִ֔ית וְלֹ֥א עָצַ֖רְתִּי כֹּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And I was left, I alone, and I saw the vision the great this, and not remained in me strength, and my vigor was changed on me to ruin, and not I retained strength.
pieces: So I was left alone, gazing at this great vision. I had no strength left; my face turned deathly pale, and I was helpless.

L.8: So I was left alone and saw this great vision, and no strength remained in me; my vigor was turned to ruin in me, and I retained no strength.

R.8: So I was left alone, looking at this great vision. I had no strength left. My face turned very pale, and I felt completely weak.

decisions.choice: my vigor was turned to ruin: my healthy look was gone, I grew deathly pale
decisions.reason: The word for vigor means splendor or a healthy look (Isaiah 53:2, "majesty"). It was "turned to destruction": the color drained from his face, as in 7:28.

decisions.choice: my face turned deathly pale (B); my face turned very pale (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1).

records.source: וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע אֶת־ק֣וֹל דְּבָרָ֑יו וּכְשָׁמְעִי֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל דְּבָרָ֔יו וַאֲנִ֗י הָיִ֛יתִי נִרְדָּ֥ם עַל־פָּנַ֖י וּפָנַ֥י אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard the sound of his words, I was dazed on my face, and my face to the ground.
pieces: Then I heard him speaking, and as I listened to the sound of his words, I fell into a deep sleep, face down, with my face to the ground.

L.9: Then I heard the sound of his words; and as I heard the sound of his words, I sank into a deep sleep on my face, my face to the ground.

R.9: Then I heard him speaking. As I listened to his voice, I fainted and lay with my face on the ground.

decisions.choice: I fell into a deep sleep on my face: as in 8:18
decisions.reason: The same word is used in 8:18 when Gabriel spoke to Daniel. He was overcome and lost consciousness.

decisions.choice: I fainted (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:18, Readable says what the deep sleep was.

records.source: וְהִנֵּה־יָ֖ד נָ֣גְעָה בִּ֑י וַתְּנִיעֵ֥נִי עַל־בִּרְכַּ֖י וְכַפּ֥וֹת יָדָֽי׃
records.gloss: And look, a hand touched me, and it set me trembling on my knees and the palms of my hands.
pieces: Then a hand touched me and raised me, trembling, onto my hands and knees.

L.10: And look, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my knees and the palms of my hands.

R.10: Suddenly a hand touched me. It helped me get up on my hands and knees, though I was shaking.

decisions.choice: set me trembling: shook me up, raised me trembling
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone shake, and here also to rouse him: the hand shakes Daniel awake and raises him onto his hands and knees, still trembling.

decisions.choice: set me, trembling, on my hands and knees (B); helped me get up ... though I was shaking (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep both parts of the verb's sense (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֡י דָּנִיֵּ֣אל אִישׁ־חֲ֠מֻדוֹת הָבֵ֨ן בַּדְּבָרִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר֩ אָנֹכִ֨י דֹבֵ֤ר אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ וַעֲמֹ֣ד עַל־עָמְדֶ֔ךָ כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה שֻׁלַּ֣חְתִּי אֵלֶ֑יךָ וּבְדַבְּר֥וֹ עִמִּ֛י אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה עָמַ֥דְתִּי מַרְעִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And he said to me: Daniel, man of preciousnesses, understand the words which I am speaking to you, and stand on your place, for now I have been sent to you. And when he spoke with me this word, I stood up trembling.
pieces: He said to me, "Daniel, you are greatly loved. Pay attention to the words I am about to speak to you, and stand up, for I have been sent to you." When he said this to me, I stood up, trembling.

L.11: And he said to me, "Daniel, man greatly loved, understand the words that I am speaking to you, and stand upright, for now I have been sent to you." And when he spoke this word to me, I stood up trembling.

R.11: He said to me, "Daniel, God loves you very much. Listen carefully to what I am going to tell you. Stand up, because I have been sent to you." When he said this to me, I stood up. I was still shaking.

decisions.choice: man greatly loved: a man treasured by God
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used of Daniel in 9:23 ("you are greatly loved") and again in verse 19. It is God who treasures him, and the messenger brings God's word.

decisions.choice: stand on your place: stand up where you are
decisions.reason: The same words as in 8:18: get up on your feet.

decisions.choice: God loves you very much (R)
decisions.reason: As in 9:23, Readable says who loves Daniel.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַי֮ אַל־תִּירָ֣א דָנִיֵּאל֒ כִּ֣י׀מִן־הַיּ֣וֹם הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧תָּ אֶֽת־לִבְּךָ֛ לְהָבִ֧ין וּלְהִתְעַנּ֛וֹת לִפְנֵ֥י אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נִשְׁמְע֣וּ דְבָרֶ֑יךָ וַאֲנִי־בָ֖אתִי בִּדְבָרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And he said to me: Do not fear, Daniel, for from the day the first that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.
pieces: Then he said to me, "Do not be afraid, Daniel. From the first day that you set your mind to gain understanding and humbled yourself before your God, your words were heard, and it is in answer to them that I have come.

L.12: And he said to me, "Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you gave your heart to understanding and to humbling yourself before your God, your words have been heard, and I have come because of your words.

R.12: Then he said to me, "Do not be afraid, Daniel. From the first day you decided to understand and to humble yourself before your God, God heard your prayers. I have come because of your prayers.

decisions.choice: humble yourself: by fasting and prayer
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the humbling of oneself by fasting on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29, 31; Psalm 35:13). Daniel's three weeks of fasting (verses 2-3) were such a humbling.

decisions.choice: you set your heart: you made up your mind, gave yourself to
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of the will and thought.

decisions.choice: God heard your prayers (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who heard and says that Daniel's "words" were his prayers. The messenger's speech runs to the end of verse 14.

records.source: וְשַׂ֣ר׀מַלְכ֣וּת פָּרַ֗ס עֹמֵ֤ד לְנֶגְדִּי֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וְאֶחָ֣ד י֔וֹם וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִֽיכָאֵ֗ל אַחַ֛ד הַשָּׂרִ֥ים הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים בָּ֣א לְעָזְרֵ֑נִי וַאֲנִי֙ נוֹתַ֣רְתִּי שָׁ֔ם אֵ֖צֶל מַלְכֵ֥י פָרָֽס׃
records.gloss: And [the] prince of [the] kingdom of Persia [was] standing before me twenty and one days; and look, Michael, one of the princes the chief, came to help me; and I, I was left there beside the kings of Persia.
pieces: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood in my way for twenty-one days, until Michael, one of the chief princes, came to my aid, because I had been left there alone with the kings of Persia.

L.13: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia was standing against me for twenty-one days; and look, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to my help, since I had been left there with the kings of Persia.

R.13: But the ruling angel of the kingdom of Persia stood against me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the most important ruling angels, came to help me. I had been left there alone with the kings of Persia.

decisions.choice: the prince of the kingdom of Persia: a heavenly power set over Persia
decisions.reason: This prince opposes God's messenger for three weeks, the length of Daniel's fast (verse 2), and Michael, a heavenly prince, comes to help. So this prince is usually understood as a spiritual being, an angelic power linked with the kingdom of Persia, as "the prince of Greece" is with Greece (verse 20). The idea that the nations have heavenly rulers is found also in Deuteronomy 32:8 in some ancient witnesses, and in Isaiah 24:21. Some read the prince as the human king of Persia, but the battle with Michael makes that hard. The text gives no more detail.

decisions.choice: Michael, one of the chief princes: the angel who stands for Israel
decisions.reason: Michael's name means "Who is like God?". In Daniel he is "your prince" (verse 21) and "the great prince who stands over your people" (12:1). Jude 9 calls him the archangel, and in Revelation 12:7 he and his angels fight the dragon.

decisions.choice: I had been left there with the kings of Persia
alternatives: I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of Persia
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "I was left there with the kings of Persia", meaning the messenger was held back alone there until Michael came. Some ancient translations read "I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of Persia", which says that Michael took over the struggle. The sense of the passage is the same.

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruling angel (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "prince" at Literal and Balanced and "ruling angel" at Readable for the word sar where it names an angel. Readable says what kind of prince is meant, since a reader would otherwise think of a human prince; that the princes of Persia and Greece are angels is the usual reading but not certain (see the meaning decision at 10:13).

records.source: וּבָ֨אתִי֙ לַהֲבִ֣ינְךָ֔ אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרָ֥ה לְעַמְּךָ֖ בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֑ים כִּי־ע֥וֹד חָז֖וֹן לַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people at the end of the days, for still [the] vision [is] for the days.
pieces: Now I have come to help you understand what will happen to your people in the days to come, for the vision concerns a time yet to come."

L.14: And I have come to give you understanding of what will befall your people at the end of the days, for there is still a vision for those days."

R.14: Now I have come to help you understand what will happen to your people in the future. The vision is about a time that has not yet come."

decisions.choice: the end of the days: the days to come, the latter days
decisions.reason: The phrase means the future, often the time when God completes his purposes (Genesis 49:1; Isaiah 2:2; Daniel 2:28). Here it covers the events of chapter 11 and the end of 12:1-3.

decisions.choice: in the days to come (B); in the future (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the end of the days"; Balanced and Readable say it plainly. Literal's "there is still a vision for those days" follows the Hebrew word order.

records.source: וּבְדַבְּר֣וֹ עִמִּ֔י כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה נָתַ֧תִּי פָנַ֛י אַ֖רְצָה וְנֶאֱלָֽמְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And when he spoke with me according to the words these, I set my face to the ground and I was dumb.
pieces: While he was saying these things to me, I bowed with my face toward the ground and could not speak.

L.15: And when he had spoken with me according to these words, I turned my face toward the ground and was speechless.

R.15: While he was saying these things to me, I bowed down with my face toward the ground. I could not say a word.

decisions.choice: I set my face toward the ground: I bowed my head low
decisions.reason: Daniel lowers his face before the heavenly speaker, overwhelmed, as in 8:18.

decisions.choice: could not speak (B); could not say a word (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be struck dumb.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֗ה כִּדְמוּת֙ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם נֹגֵ֖עַ עַל־שְׂפָתָ֑י וָאֶפְתַּח־פִּ֗י וָאֲדַבְּרָה֙ וָאֹֽמְרָה֙ אֶל־הָעֹמֵ֣ד לְנֶגְדִּ֔י אֲדֹנִ֗י בַּמַּרְאָה֙ נֶהֶפְכ֤וּ צִירַי֙ עָלַ֔י וְלֹ֥א עָצַ֖רְתִּי כֹּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And look, [one] like [the] likeness of [the] sons of man touching my lips; and I opened my mouth and spoke and said to the [one] standing before me: My lord, by the vision my pangs have turned on me, and not I have retained strength.
pieces: Then one who looked like a human being touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and began to speak. I said to the one standing in front of me, "My lord, the vision has overwhelmed me with anguish, and I have no strength left.

L.16: And look, one in the likeness of the sons of man was touching my lips; and I opened my mouth and spoke, and said to the one standing in front of me, "My lord, at the vision pangs have come upon me, and I have retained no strength.

R.16: Then someone who looked like a human being touched my lips. I opened my mouth and began to speak. I said to the one standing in front of me, "Sir, the vision has filled me with pain, and I have no strength left.

decisions.choice: one in the likeness of the sons of man: one who looked human
decisions.reason: "Sons of man" means human beings. The phrase is a hedged description of a heavenly being in human form, like "one with the appearance of a man" in 8:15 and "one like a son of man" in 7:13. It is probably the same messenger as in verses 10-14.

decisions.choice: touched my lips: so that he could speak
decisions.reason: Compare Isaiah 6:7, where a seraph touches the prophet's lips, and Jeremiah 1:9. Daniel, struck dumb (verse 15), is enabled to speak.

decisions.choice: my lord: a polite address to a superior
decisions.reason: Daniel addresses the messenger as "my lord" (adoni), the respectful address used to a king or master (Genesis 24:18; 1 Samuel 25:24). It is not the title used for God.

decisions.choice: pangs: pains like those of childbirth
decisions.reason: The word is used of the pains of a woman in labor (1 Samuel 4:19; Isaiah 21:3). The vision has gripped Daniel with anguish.

decisions.choice: my lord (L, B); Sir (R); lowercase
decisions.reason: The address is lowercase, since it is said to a heavenly messenger (m3). Readable says "Sir", a polite address in plain English. Literal keeps "the sons of man"; Balanced and Readable say "a human being", as the table does for 7:13 at Readable.

records.source: וְהֵ֣יךְ יוּכַ֗ל עֶ֤בֶד אֲדֹנִי֙ זֶ֔ה לְדַבֵּ֖ר עִם־אֲדֹ֣נִי זֶ֑ה וַאֲנִ֤י מֵעַ֨תָּה֙ לֹֽא־יַעֲמָד־בִּ֣י כֹ֔חַ וּנְשָׁמָ֖ה לֹ֥א נִשְׁאֲרָה־בִֽי׃
records.gloss: And how is able the servant of this my lord to speak with this my lord? And I, from now not remains in me strength, and breath not is left in me.
pieces: How can I, your servant, speak with you, my lord? My strength is gone, and I can hardly breathe."

L.17: How can this servant of my lord speak with this my lord? As for me, from now on no strength remains in me, and no breath is left in me."

R.17: Sir, I am your servant. How can I talk with you? I have no strength left, and I can hardly breathe."

decisions.choice: this servant of my lord: I, your servant
decisions.reason: Daniel speaks of himself in the third person, as a servant speaks to a master (Genesis 44:18-19). The repeated "this" stresses the gulf between the two.

decisions.choice: servant (all levels)
decisions.reason: Daniel calls himself the messenger's servant out of politeness; every level keeps "servant", as in 9:17. Balanced and Readable turn the third person into "I" and "you" (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֧סֶף וַיִּגַּע־בִּ֛י כְּמַרְאֵ֥ה אָדָ֖ם וַֽיְחַזְּקֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And he again touched me, [one] like [the] appearance of man, and he strengthened me.
pieces: Again the one who looked like a human being touched me and gave me strength.

L.18: And again one with the appearance of a man touched me and strengthened me.

R.18: Again the one who looked like a human being touched me. He made me strong again.

decisions.choice: one with the appearance of a man: the messenger in human form
decisions.reason: As in verse 16 and 8:15. The word for "man" here is the general word for a human being.

decisions.choice: a man (L); a human being (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "a man" for the word adam here; Balanced and Readable say "a human being", as in verse 16.

records.source: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אַל־תִּירָ֧א אִישׁ־חֲמֻד֛וֹת שָׁל֥וֹם לָ֖ךְ חֲזַ֣ק וַחֲזָ֑ק וּֽבְדַבְּר֤וֹעִמִּי֙ הִתְחַזַּ֔קְתִּי וָאֹֽמְרָ֛ה יְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲדֹנִ֖י כִּ֥י חִזַּקְתָּֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And he said: Do not fear, man of preciousnesses; peace to you; be strong, and be strong. And when he spoke with me, I strengthened myself and said: Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.
pieces: He said, "Do not be afraid, you who are greatly loved. Peace be with you. Be strong; be strong!" As he spoke to me, I grew stronger and said, "Speak, my lord, for you have given me strength."

L.19: And he said, "Do not fear, man greatly loved. Peace be to you; be strong, yes, be strong." And as he spoke with me, I grew strong and said, "Let my lord speak, since you have given me strength."

R.19: He said, "Do not be afraid. God loves you very much. Peace be with you. Be strong. Be strong!" As he spoke to me, I became stronger. Then I said, "Sir, please speak, because you have made me strong."

decisions.choice: peace to you; be strong, be strong: words of comfort and courage
decisions.reason: "Peace to you" is a greeting and a reassurance (Judges 6:23). The doubled "be strong" is the charge given to Joshua (Joshua 1:6-9) and to Solomon (1 Chronicles 28:20).

decisions.choice: peace (all levels)
decisions.reason: Shalom is "peace" at every level, as in the Isaiah table.

decisions.choice: God loves you very much (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲיָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ לָמָּה־בָּ֣אתִי אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְעַתָּ֣ה אָשׁ֔וּב לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עִם־שַׂ֣ר פָּרָ֑ס וַאֲנִ֣י יוֹצֵ֔א וְהִנֵּ֥ה שַׂר־יָוָ֖ן בָּֽא׃
records.gloss: And he said: Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight with [the] prince of Persia; and I am going out, and look, [the] prince of Greece will come.
pieces: He said, "Do you know why I came to you? Now I must return to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I am done with him, the prince of Greece will come.

L.20: And he said, "Do you know why I came to you? And now I will go back to fight against the prince of Persia; and when I go out, look, the prince of Greece will come.

R.20: He said, "Do you know why I have come to you? Soon I must go back to fight against the ruling angel of Persia. When I have finished with him, the ruling angel of Greece will come.

decisions.choice: when I go out: when I have finished with Persia, or when I go out to battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to go out. It may mean that when the messenger leaves the fight with Persia, Greece's prince will come, as Greece followed Persia in history (8:20-21); or that when he goes out to battle, Greece's prince will come as well. The first fits the order of kingdoms in chapters 8 and 11.

decisions.choice: the prince of Persia, the prince of Greece: heavenly powers behind the nations
decisions.reason: As in verse 13. The struggle of nations on earth is shown with a struggle in heaven behind it.

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruling angel (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "prince" at Literal and Balanced and "ruling angel" at Readable for the word sar where it names an angel. Readable says what kind of prince is meant, since a reader would otherwise think of a human prince; that the princes of Persia and Greece are angels is the usual reading but not certain (see the meaning decision at 10:13).

records.source: אֲבָל֙ אַגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ אֶת־הָרָשׁ֥וּם בִּכְתָ֖ב אֱמֶ֑ת וְאֵ֨ין אֶחָ֜ד מִתְחַזֵּ֤ק עִמִּי֙ עַל־אֵ֔לֶּה כִּ֥י אִם־מִיכָאֵ֖ל שַׂרְכֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: But I will tell you what is inscribed in [the] writing of truth; and there is not one showing himself strong with me against these, except Michael your prince.
pieces: But first I will tell you what is written in the book of truth. No one supports me against them except Michael, your prince.

L.21: But I will tell you what has been inscribed in the writing of truth. There is no one who stands firmly with me against these except Michael, your prince.

R.21: But first I will tell you what is written in the Book of Truth. No one helps me fight against them except Michael, the ruling angel who watches over your people.

decisions.choice: the book of truth: the heavenly record of what God has decreed
decisions.reason: The "writing of truth" is the record of God's plan, which the messenger now reveals. Compare the books of 7:10 and 12:1, and the sealed scroll of Revelation 5:1.

decisions.choice: Michael, your prince: the heavenly protector of Daniel's people
decisions.reason: "Your" is plural: Michael is the prince of Daniel's people, Israel, as 12:1 says.

decisions.choice: the speech runs on into chapter 11
decisions.reason: The messenger's words continue in 11:1, where he says how he stood by Darius the Mede. The chapter break falls in the middle of his speech.

decisions.choice: the ruling angel who watches over your people (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "ruling angel" for prince, as the table gives, and says whose prince Michael is (m2). It capitalizes "Book of Truth" as a title.
